lessons.title: Compiling Modern C++ and Reading Diagnostics
lessons.summary: Build a repeatable C++20 edit-compile-link-run workflow and distinguish compiler, linker, runtime, and logic failures.
objectives: Explain and apply Compiling Modern C++ and Reading Diagnostics
Compile and test behavior with observable evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Compile with a modern language mode and strict warnings, for example `c++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.cpp -o app`. Source is translated to object code and linked into an executable. Headers normally contain declarations while one or more source files provide definitions. A compiler diagnostic reports an invalid translation unit; a linker error reports a missing or duplicate definition. Read the earliest relevant message, fix one cause, rebuild, and do not run a stale executable after a failed build. Prefer standard facilities over compiler-specific extensions.

lessons.title: Values, Types, Initialization, and Streams
lessons.summary: Use fundamental and library types, brace initialization, const, explicit conversion, strings, streams, and validated input.
objectives: Explain and apply Values, Types, Initialization, and Streams
Compile and test behavior with observable evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: C++ is statically typed and supports value semantics. Brace initialization makes narrowing conversions visible. Use `const` for values that should not change and `auto` when the initializer makes the exact type clear, not to hide an important contract. Integer division discards a fractional part; convert an operand before division. `std::string` manages text storage safely. Stream extraction reports failure through stream state, so validate `std::cin` before using the destination value. Prefer explicit conversions and avoid C-style casts.

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Conditions use `bool`, and `&&` plus `||` short-circuit. Place validity checks before dependent expressions such as division or indexing. Use `if` chains for ranges and `switch` for discrete integral or enumeration values. Every case should terminate intentionally with `break`, `return`, or a documented fallthrough. Keep variables in the smallest useful scope. Do not confuse assignment with equality, and enable warnings that identify suspicious conditions. Test immediately below, at, and above each threshold.

lessons.title: Loops, std::array, and std::vector
lessons.summary: Traverse fixed and dynamic sequences with range-for and indexed loops while preserving bounds, iterator validity, and accumulator invariants.
objectives: Explain and apply Loops, std::array, and std::vector
Compile and test behavior with observable evidence

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: `std::array<T,N>` represents a fixed-size sequence and `std::vector<T>` owns a dynamically sized contiguous sequence. Prefer range-based `for` when only values matter and use a reference when mutation is intentional. `size()` returns an unsigned size type; use consistent index types. `at()` checks bounds and throws, while `operator[]` requires the caller to guarantee a valid index. Adding to a vector can invalidate iterators, pointers, and references, so do not grow it while traversing through those handles. Standard algorithms often express intent more clearly than manual loops.

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: Arguments are passed by value unless a reference type is declared. Use `const T&` for read-only access to a potentially expensive object and `T&` for deliberate caller-visible mutation. Return values are usually clear and efficiently optimized. A class should keep fields private and establish invariants in its constructor. RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime: containers, strings, file streams, and smart pointers release resources through destructors. Prefer these owners over manual `new` and `delete`. Mark member functions `const` when they do not modify observable state.

objectives: Explain and apply STL Algorithms, Maps, and a Progress Tracker

blocks.heading: Core model
blocks.bodyMarkdown: The standard library provides containers, iterators, algorithms, and resource-managing types. `std::map` associates ordered unique keys with values; `std::unordered_map` provides hash-based lookup without sorted iteration. Algorithms such as `std::find_if`, `std::count_if`, and `std::accumulate` separate traversal from intent. Lambdas provide local callable behavior and should capture only what they need. File streams close automatically through RAII, but open, read, and write state must still be checked. Parse persisted data as untrusted input before constructing valid domain objects.
